story.titleZh: 阿隆索批评F1下游车手质量引发争议
story.summaryZh: 阿隆索在美国大奖赛后称F1排名后三分之一的车手质量很低，并在墨西哥站再次批评并点名阿尔本，多位车手则为阿尔本辩护。
story.originalTitle: What Fernando Alonso is getting wrong about F1 driving standards
story.summaryEn: Fernando Alonso said after the United States Grand Prix that the quality of drivers in the lower third of the grid is very low, and he doubled down in Mexico by singling out Alex Albon, while several drivers spoke up in Albon's defence.
detailZh: 阿隆索在F1驾驶标准上错在哪里
利亚姆·劳森指出了比现役F1车手是否“配得上”席位更大的问题——进入F1本身就太难了
阿隆索在上周末奥斯汀美国大奖赛结束后宣称“排名后三分之一的车手质量非常低”，无意中捅了马蜂窝。
本周在墨西哥，阿隆索继续加码批评并点名亚历克斯·阿尔本，而许多其他车手则为这位威廉姆斯车手辩护。阿尔本本人表示：“我们不再有付费车手了。要说的话，我认为现在的发车阵容是近年来最强的。”
某位车手是否“配得上”进入一级方程式，这个问题比表面看起来要复杂得多。车手的能力与他们带来的预算之间，未必就是反比关系。以塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯为例，他为凯迪拉克车队带来了可观的赞助，但很难说他今年没有用表现证明自己的位置——他最近的续约就是明证。
但正如利亚姆·劳森在被问及对驾驶标准风波有何看法时所指出的，在单座赛车金字塔更靠下的层级，预算在制造不平等方面扮演着更大的角色。
“我认为更大的问题是，一级方程式太难进入了，”他说。
“对人们来说，成长并尝试进入F1的成本太高了。所以，我认为有很多车手永远、永远甚至都得不到机会去展示他们在赛车中能做到什么。
多年来，有很多情况下，你会说有些车手可能没那么配得上，却比其他车手获得了机会。所以，我觉得F1一直就是这样。老实说，感觉现在正越来越朝那个方向发展。
这实在太难了。进入的门槛非常非常高。现在多了两个席位是好事，但这是一项全世界只有22个席位的运动。
要进入非常非常艰难。我觉得一直以来都太难进了。这可能是更大的问题。
劳森的说法在很多方面都相当有道理。在预算帽时代，车队已经被圈护起来，本身成为了有价值的特许经营体。有些车队，比如哈斯和威廉姆斯，整体预算可能比其他车队低，或者技术基础设施较少——这是上一个时代遗留下来的问题——但他们不再像过去那样靠一场接一场比赛勉强维持。如今，能带来预算的车手是锦上添花，而不是必需品。
劳森本人受益于红牛的扶持，尽管其青训车手计划以残酷著称。
历史上，发车格上更靠前的车队自然能吸引最健康的赞助商，因为他们获得最多曝光，这让队尾车队只能依赖付费车手，而这些车手的能力往往参差不齐。这是公开的秘密。有一个关于1990年代中期付费车手里卡多·罗塞特的传闻（未必属实）：据说他习惯性地以远低于速度的圈速排位；据说疲惫的泰瑞尔机械师把他围场滑板车上的“R”和“T”对调，结果读成了“tosser”。
尽管国际汽联在排位赛中引入了107%规则以淘汰危险慢车，但由于F1政治的运作，队尾车队在2000年代可以说越来越依赖付费车手。前权利持有人伯尼·埃克莱斯顿的分而治之策略导致F1商业合同《协和协议》的 successive 版本在奖金分配上大幅偏向领先车队。
F1现在有了财务上公平得多的安排，但 feeder 方程式仍然靠现金运转——而且是大笔现金。通往F1的途径也许最好用维恩图来表达，其中各个集合包括超级富有的父母、良好的赞助商关系，和/或来自F1车队青训车手计划的一些支持。
即便是埃斯特班·奥康——他的父亲曾在卡丁车赛道翻垃圾桶，捡拾富家子弟只用过一次就丢弃的轮胎——也曾得到过路特斯和梅赛德斯的帮助。并非每个人都能在年幼时就被发掘出天赋。
“我其实没有过多去想今年发车阵容的水平，也没去想谁配得上、谁配不上这个位置，”劳森说道。
“但我觉得这项运动就是需要变得更容易进入一些。因为就连去跑卡丁车都贵得离谱。而且现在从很小的年纪就开始了——我觉得我在新西兰小时候算是躲过了这一关，我也得到了身边非常慷慨的人们的大力支持。
“但我觉得问题从很小就开始了，即便在卡丁车阶段，一个孩子有六七台引擎，而另一个孩子没法测试、没法用新轮胎。这始终是一种劣势。所以，是的，这是一项装备影响巨大的运动。”
detailEn: What Fernando Alonso is getting wrong about F1 driving standards
Liam Lawson has pointed to a bigger picture beyond the question of whether drivers currently in Formula 1 "deserve" to be there – it's too hard to reach in the first place

When Fernando Alonso declared "the quality of the drivers in the lower third of the grid is very low" in the aftermath of last weekend's United States Grand Prix in Austin, he inadvertently poked a hornets' nest.

While Alonso doubled down on his criticism this week in Mexico, singling out Alex Albon, many other drivers have spoken up in the Williams driver's defence. Albon himself said, "We don't have pay drivers anymore. If anything, I would say the grid's the strongest it's been in a while."

The issue of whether a particular driver 'deserves' to be in Formula 1 is more complex than it appears. It's not necessarily the case that there is an inverse relationship between a driver's ability and the budget they bring. Sergio Perez, for instance, brings considerable sponsorship to the Cadillac team, and yet it would be difficult to argue that he hasn't justified his position through performance this year – as evinced by his recent contract renewal.
But as Liam Lawson pointed out when asked for his take on the driving standards furore, budget plays a bigger role in creating inequalities much further down the single-seater ladder.
"I think the bigger thing is, Formula 1 is too hard to get into," he said.
"It's too expensive for people to grow up and try and get into. And so, I think there's so many drivers that will never, ever even get the chance to showcase what they can do in a race car.

"Over the years, there's been many cases of drivers who you would say probably didn't deserve it as much, getting the chance over other drivers. So, I feel like that's always been like it in Formula 1. Honestly, it feels like it's heading more in that direction.
"It's just too difficult. The access is very, very hard. It's great that there's two more seats now, but it's a sport of 22 seats in the world.
"It's very, very tough to get into. I feel like it's always just been too hard to get into. That's probably the bigger issue."

Lawson's contention is quite plausible in many ways. In the budget-cap era, the teams have been ring-fenced and become valuable franchises in their own right. Some, such as Haas and Williams, may have a lower overall budget than others or have less technical infrastructure – a hangover from the previous era – but they are no longer scraping by from race to race, as they once were. A driver who brings a budget is now a nice-to-have, rather than a necessity.
Lawson himself benefitted from Red Bull's backing, though its young-driver scheme is infamously brutal

Historically, teams further up the grid naturally attracted the healthiest sponsors since they got the most exposure, leaving the tail-enders reliant on pay drivers who often had mixed abilities. It was an open secret. There is an apocryphal story about mid-1990s pay driver Ricardo Rosset, who habitually qualified well off the pace: it's said the weary Tyrrell mechanics transposed the 'R' and the 'T' on his paddock scooter so it read "tosser".

Although the FIA brought in the 107% rule in qualifying to eliminate dangerously slow drivers, the tail-enders arguably became increasingly reliant on paying drivers through the 2000s owing to the machinations of F1 politics. Former rights holder Bernie Ecclestone's divide-and-rule tactics led to successive iterations of the Concorde Agreement, F1's commercial contract, massively favouring the leading teams in terms of prize money distribution.

F1 has a much more financially equitable arrangement now but the feeder formulae still run on cash – and lots of it. The means of getting to F1 is perhaps best expressed through a Venn diagram in which the various sets include super-rich parents, good sponsor connections, and/or some support from an F1 team's young-driver programme.

Even Esteban Ocon, whose father raided the bins at kart circuits to scavenge tyres the rich kids had used only once before discarding, had a helping hand from Lotus and Mercedes. Not everyone can be talent-spotted at an early age.
"I haven't really thought about the level of the grid this year and who does or doesn't deserve to be there," said Lawson.

"But I think the sport just needs to be somehow easier to get into. Because even like going go-kart racing is just insanely expensive. And from a very young age now – I think I got away with it as a kid in New Zealand, I also got very well supported by very generous people around me.

"But I think it starts from a young age where even in go-karts, a kid who's got six or seven engines versus a kid who can't test, can't run new tyres. It's just always a disadvantage. So, yeah, it's a sport where the gear makes a big difference."

detailZh: F1卡塔尔大奖赛：乔治·拉塞尔击败安东内利夺得杆位
乔治·拉塞尔在2026年第六次夺得杆位，梅赛德斯车队在F1卡塔尔大奖赛的预赛中全面领先。
乔治·拉塞尔在F1卡塔尔大奖赛中夺得杆位，击败队友安东内利，梅赛德斯车队在多哈的比赛中全面领先。
在卢塞尔赛道的高下压力赛道上，梅赛德斯车队在周末的每一节练习中都证明了自己比竞争对手更胜一筹，并通过利用其转向优势锁定了前两排。
拉塞尔在决定性的Q3冲刺赛中，在第一轮和第二轮中分别跑出1m21.695s的成绩，领先他的世界冠军队友近两十分，并且明显领先其他竞争者。
安东内利质疑自己为何在最后一轮中排在第一位，这位意大利少年在第二次尝试中找不到任何改进，最终排名第二。拉塞尔几乎复制了他的第一次成绩，但无需改进就赢得了他本赛季第六个杆位，这对于他的成长之旅意义重大。
迈凯轮的兰多·诺里斯在第二轮中提高了十分，以第三名的成绩领先队友奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里，而伊萨克·哈吉亚在排位赛中击败了他的红牛队友马克斯·维斯塔潘，获得了第五个发车位。
法拉利在多哈的糟糕周末继续，整个练习赛中都在为抓地力和速度而挣扎。查尔斯·勒克莱尔只能排在第七位，距离杆位有1.260秒的差距。青训车队小红牛的菜鸟车手阿维德·林德布拉德击败了刘易斯·汉密尔顿的第二辆法拉利，利亚姆·劳森以第十名的成绩结束了前十。
红牛车队在Q2的表现与梅赛德斯车队相当接近，哈德贾的成绩为1m22.344s，比领跑者拉塞尔慢不到三十分之一，拉塞尔以1m22.079s的成绩领先安东内利。
在这两支车队和梅赛德斯车队之后，法拉利再次陷入困境，勒克莱尔落后整整一秒，他们试图与小红牛车队抗衡。
尽管如此，两队仍有足够的余地进入Q3。对于前十名的争夺，哈斯、阿尔派和奥迪之间的竞争非常激烈，但最终这三支车队都没有足够的实力去威胁排名第十的劳森。
奥利弗·贝尔曼最接近，只差0.240s未能晋级。皮埃尔·加斯利从FP2中失去的时间中恢复过来，在发车位上获得第十二名，随后是加布里埃尔·博托莱托和他的队友弗朗哥·科拉平托。哈斯车队的新人拉斐尔·卡马拉和经验丰富的尼科·胡肯伯格将在周日的第八排发车。
梅赛德斯和红牛是唯一两支在Q1中只完成了一圈计时圈速的车队，拉塞尔的1分22.557秒领先，排在安东内利和维斯塔潘之前。其他领跑者虽然也在磨损的轮胎上完成了一圈，但同样也为稍后保留了关键的软胎。
第一轮练习结束后，卡洛斯·塞恩斯和亚历克斯·阿隆诺在圈外观望，威廉姆斯车手在第二轮练习后仍保持在这个位置。这对科拉平托来说是个安慰，他凭借0.1秒的优势从第16位惊险晋级Q1。与此同时，哈斯车队的新人卡马拉也晋级到第14位，但他为此不得不使用第二套软胎。
费尔南多·阿隆索和兰斯·斯特罗尔分别以第19位和第20位为陷入困境的阿斯顿·马丁车队挣扎，凯迪拉克车队的瓦尔特里·博塔斯和塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯完成了周日的排位赛。
detailEn: F1 Qatar GP: George Russell beats Kimi Antonelli to pole
George Russell takes sixth pole of 2026 as Mercedes dominates qualifying at Formula 1's Qatar Grand Prix
George Russell has grabbed an emphatic pole for Formula 1's Qatar Grand Prix, defeating team-mate Kimi Antonelli as Mercedes blitzed the competition in Doha.

On the demanding, high-downforce circuit of Lusail, Mercedes proved a step ahead of the competition in every session over the weekend, and the Silver Arrows capitalised on their cornering advantage by locking out the front row.
Russell led from Antonelli after the first of two runs in the decisive Q3 shootout with a 1m21.695s lap, nearly two tenths up on his world champion team-mate and well clear of the competition.

As Antonelli questioned being out first in the queue for the final runs, the Italian teenager struggled to find any improvement on his second attempt and settled for second. Russell almost matched his first run, but did not need to improve to claim his sixth pole of a character-building campaign.
McLaren's Lando Norris found a tenth on his second lap to claim third ahead of team-mate Oscar Piastri, with Isack Hadjar out-qualifying his Red Bull team-mate Max Verstappen for fifth on the grid.

Ferrari continued a woeful weekend in Doha, having been struggling for grip and pace throughout practice. Charles Leclerc could only manage seventh on the grid, a shocking 1.260s off pole. Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad beat the second Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton to eighth, with Liam Lawson rounding out the top 10.
Red Bull, rather than McLaren, looked somewhat close to Mercedes in Q2, with Hadjar's 1m22.344s less than three tenths behind pacesetter Russell, who had the edge on Antonelli with a 1m22.079s lap.
Behind those two teams and McLaren, Ferrari struggled again, with Leclerc a full second behind as they looked to fight with Racing Bulls.

There was still a big enough cushion for both teams to make it into Q3, though. The battle for the top-10 was a tight fight between Haas, Alpine and Audi, but ultimately none of the three teams had enough in the tank to bother 10th-placed Lawson.

Oliver Bearman came closest, missing the cut by 0.240s. Pierre Gasly recovered from lost track time in FP2 to take 12th on the grid, followed by Gabriel Bortoleto and team-mate Franco Colapinto. Haas rookie Rafael Camara and veteran Nico Hulkenberg will start from the eighth row on Sunday.

Mercedes and Red Bull were the only two teams to just set one timed lap in Q1, with Russell's 1m22.557s leading the way ahead of Antonelli and Verstappen. The other frontrunners set a second time on scrubbed tyres, though, equally saving crucial sets of softs for later on.

After the first set of runs, Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon were on the outside looking in and the Williams drivers stayed in those positions after the second effort. That was a relief for Colapinto, who escaped Q1 by a tenth of a second in 16th. Meanwhile, Haas rookie Camara also advanced in 14th, but had to deploy a second set of softs to do so in 14th.
Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll were 19th and 20th for struggling Aston Martin, with Cadillac duo Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez completing Sunday's grid.

detailZh: F1卡塔尔大奖赛：Kimi安东内利完成排位赛练习全胜，梅赛德斯占据巨大优势
Kimi安东内利和乔治·拉塞尔在F1卡塔尔大奖赛的最后一场练习赛中展示了梅赛德斯车队的强大实力
Kimi安东内利为梅赛德斯车队在卡塔尔大奖赛的练习赛中赢得了全胜，银箭车队带着巨大优势进入排位赛
乔治·拉塞尔在半程之前速度最快，各车队开始进行软胎测试，但安东内利在下半场再次缩短了圈速
不同于周五两次红旗的FP2练习，第三场练习没有发生任何事故，这在很大程度上要归功于一个平淡的开局，早期几乎没有动作。一开始，皮埃尔·加斯利独自一人绕赛道行驶，这是在周五第二场练习中他的阿尔派赛车在中途翻车后，弥补失去的地盘。
加斯利最终被队友弗朗哥·科拉平托和凯迪拉克的瓦尔特里·博塔加入，而其他人则在练习的前三分之一时间里待在维修区。
但在20分钟之前，情况突然发生了变化，重量级的赛车手们开始了软胎的练习——这种轮胎预计只对排位赛有用。比赛预计将在中胎和硬胎的Pirelli轮胎上完成，这些轮胎在卢塞尔赛道上面临最严峻的周末。随着排位赛模拟的开始，即将离任的世界冠军兰多·诺里斯在遭遇剧烈的过度转向后，驶向了14号弯的逃生道路。
正如周五两次练习的情况一样，梅赛德斯车队立即掌控了局面，乔治·拉塞尔以1分22.983秒的成绩领先队友基米·安东内利。这比麦克拉伦的奥斯卡·皮亚斯蒂和马克斯·维斯塔潘能做出的成绩快了半秒以上，后者驾驶的雷诺红牛小红牛22赛车在更艰难的自由练习后需要重新平衡。
虽然拉塞尔随后在5号弯道漂移过宽，安东内利的第二次中期练习跑出的成绩几乎与队友相同，仅慢了0.017秒。
在还剩15分钟的时候，维斯塔潘短暂地占据了领先位置，但安东内利立即反击，并以1分22.400秒的成绩为梅赛德斯车队恢复了半秒的领先优势。拉塞尔对此速度的爆发毫无应对之策，落后了0.249秒。
维斯塔潘仍然排在第三位，作为第一辆非梅赛德斯车队赛车，落后0.501秒，其后是他的队友伊萨克·哈德贾。
在查尔斯·勒克莱尔将其描述为“非常困难”的周五之后，法拉利车队几乎没有取得进步，勒克莱尔排名第五，落后安东内利八十分之一秒。迈凯轮车队的表现也超过了预期，诺里斯排名第六，皮亚斯特里排名第七。
汉密尔顿在最后的练习圈中被交通堵塞，表现不如预期，最终在第九位完成了比赛，分开了小红牛的中场领跑者阿维德·林德布拉德和利亚姆·劳森。
detailEn: F1 Qatar GP: Kimi Antonelli completes practice clean sweep as Mercedes dominates
Kimi Antonelli and George Russell showcase Mercedes' dominant form in final practice for Formula 1's Qatar Grand Prix
Kimi Antonelli has handed Mercedes a clean sweep of Qatar GP practice sessions as the Silver Arrows head to qualifying with a huge advantage.

Russell went quickest before halfway as teams embarked on soft-tyre runs with Mercedes continuing its ominous form on the high-downforce motorcycle circuit of Lusail, only for Antonelli to take another chunk out of that laptime in the second half.

Unlike Friday's twice red-flagged FP2 session, third practice took place without incident, which was partly thanks to a tepid start with little to no action early on. At the start, Pierre Gasly circulated by himself, making up for lost ground after beaching his Alpine in the gravel midway through Friday's second practice.
Gasly was eventually joined by team-mate Franco Colapinto and Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas, while the others stayed in the garage for the first third of the session.

That all changed suddenly before the 20-minute mark as the heavy hitters embarked on soft-tyre runs - a compound projected to be only useful for qualifying. The race is expected to be completed on medium and hard Pirelli tyres, which are facing their most demanding weekend on the Lusail loop. As qualifying simulations got underway, outgoing world champion Lando Norris headed to the Turn 14 escape road after catching a violent snap of oversteer.

As was the case during both of Friday's practice endeavours, Mercedes immediately took charge with George Russell's 1m22.983s leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli. That was over half a second better than what McLaren's Oscar Piastri and Max Verstappen could muster, the latter driving a Red Bull RB22 which required rebalancing after a tougher free practice outing.
While Russell then drifted wide in Turn 5, Antonelli's second mid-session run yielded a time almost identical to his team-mate's, just 0.017s off.

With 15 minutes to go, Verstappen briefly claimed top before Antonelli immediately retaliated and restored Mercedes' comfortable half-second cushion with a 1m22.400s effort. Russell had no answer for that flash of pace, conceding 0.249s.
Verstappen remained third, a sobering 0.501s in arrears as the first non-Mercedes car, followed by team-mate Isack Hadjar.

After a Friday which Charles Leclerc described as "very difficult", there was little progress for Ferrari as Leclerc took fifth, eight tenths behind Antonelli. McLaren also struggled more than was expected with sixth for Norris and seventh for Piastri.
Lewis Hamilton fared worse after being held up by traffic on his final hotlap, splitting Racing Bull's midfield leaders Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson in ninth.

detailZh: 国际汽联探索在F1 V8引擎中恢复DRS系统并推动通过系统
独家对Motorsport.com发表谈话，国际汽联单座赛车总监Nikolas Tombazis透露了管理机构如何能在2030年结合空气动力学和电气超越辅助系统
上周宣布的框架确立了下个一级方程式动力单元法规的关键要素——一个2.1升涡轮增压V8，其电气组件显著减少——但在接下来的几个月里，仍有许多细节需要完善
其中关键未解决的问题是如何促进超越。对于2026年，国际汽联引入了超越模式，但这主要是由于这套规则设定极其复杂的结果。
为了使当前的动力单元规定能够有效实施，汽车需要具有显著更低的阻力，这就是为什么引入了带有直线模式区域的主动空气动力学。由于每位车手都可以打开前后翼片，DRS作为超越辅助工具消失了，国际汽联不得不提出一个替代方案，结果就是超越模式。
目标是使下一轮规则周期中的整个概念大大简化。国际汽联单座赛车总监尼科拉斯·托马齐斯在接受Motorsport.com独家采访时确认，直线模式（SM）区域将消失，并且管理机构正在研究更熟悉的概念。
幕后，目前正在努力确定从2030年起在超越辅助工具方面需要什么。国际汽联正在调查几个选项，包括推杆加速和DRS的组合。
“在比赛条件下，电能将肯定更多地集中在推杆加速上，而较少地集中在能量回收上。由于与当前引擎相比，电能部分在尺寸上会小得多，这意味着所有与能量使用相关的规定都将被消除或大幅简化，”托马齐斯告诉Motorsport.com。
“所以是的，这将是超车的基本点，但我们仍在进行超车和近距离比赛的模拟。”
“这些模拟旨在确定在推杆加速方面需要什么——是像IndyCar那样的每场比赛固定秒数，还是不同的系统——以及是否需要与DRS的回归相结合。”
“如果我们需要添加DRS并与一些电气部件一起使用，我们将非常乐意这样做，”Tombazis说。”
“只是想说明：在下一项规定下，我们不再需要SM模式区域，因此我们将保留拥有更多类似DRS的设备来补充电气部件的选项，以确保我们有正确的近距离比赛水平。”
机械师正在对马克斯·维斯塔潘的小红牛18赛车DRS系统进行维修
虽然正在进行模拟，但尚未确认推杆和DRS是否会真正结合，尽管托马齐斯确认这种结合现在已经在考虑之中。
“可能会，是的。我没有说它将完全那样，但确实可能会有DRS和推杆两种功能。”
根据最初的提案，电气组件将提供高达200kW的动力，其中100kW用于正常使用，另外100kW用于推杆加速。
通过可能将DRS添加到其中，国际汽联希望找到正确的平衡：超车动作理想情况下应该再次在刹车区域完成，而不是在直道的一半处。
"是的，我想说的是，DRS是解决这个问题的已知方案。这不像是我们需要发明的东西。我们只需要看看，A，我们是否需要它，B，我们需要多少。"
"我们显然不希望出现一种情况，即汽车毫无竞争地飞驰而过，我们希望有比赛。我们希望汽车进入弯道时并排而行，并展开竞争，但我们有工具基本上以正确的方式调整它，以适应2030年。"
detailEn: FIA explores DRS return alongside push-to-pass system for F1’s V8 engines
Speaking exclusively to Motorsport.com, FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis reveals how the governing body could combine aerodynamic and electrical overtaking aids in 2030

Although the framework announced last week establishes the key elements of Formula 1’s next power unit regulations – a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 with a significantly reduced electrical component – many details still need to be worked out over the coming months.
One of the key remaining questions is how to facilitate overtaking. For 2026, the FIA introduced overtake mode, but that is primarily a consequence of how incredibly complex this ruleset is.

For the current power unit regulations to work, the cars needed to have considerably less drag, which is why active aerodynamics were introduced with straight mode zones. With every driver able to open their front and rear wings, DRS disappeared as an overtaking aid and the FIA had to come up with an alternative, which turned out to be overtake mode.

The aim is to keep the whole concept considerably simpler for the next rules cycle. FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis confirmed in an exclusive interview with Motorsport.com that straight mode (SM) zones will disappear and that the governing body is looking into more familiar concepts.

Behind the scenes, work is currently underway to establish what will be needed in terms of overtaking aids from 2030 onwards. The FIA is investigating several options, including a combination of push-to-pass and DRS.

"The electrical power in race conditions will definitely be more focused on push-to-pass and less on the energy recovery. Because the electrical part will be so much smaller in dimensions compared to the current engines, it means that all the regulations that relate to the energy usage will be either eliminated or hugely simplified," Tombazis told Motorsport.com.
"So yeah, it will be a fundamental point for overtaking, but we are still doing simulations about overtaking and close racing."

Those simulations are intended to establish exactly what is needed in terms of push-to-pass – a fixed number of seconds per race, as IndyCar has, or a different system – and also whether it needs to be combined with the return of DRS.
"If we need to have an addition of DRS to go together with some electrical part, then we will be more than happy to do that," Tombazis said.

"And just to say: we won't need to have SM mode zones anymore under the next regulations, and therefore we would retain the option to have a more DRS-like device to complement the electrical part to make sure that we have the right level of close racing."
Mechanics work on the DRS of Max Verstappen, Red Bull RB18
While simulations are ongoing, it has not yet been confirmed that push-to-pass and DRS will indeed be combined, although Tombazis did confirm that such a combination is now on the table.
"It could be, yes. I didn't say that it will be exactly like that, but yeah, there could be both [DRS and push-to-pass]."
Under the initial proposal, the electrical component would deliver up to 200kW, with 100kW available for normal use and the other 100kW for push-to-pass.
By potentially adding DRS to that, the FIA wants to strike the right balance: overtaking moves should ideally once again be completed in the braking zone rather than halfway down a straight.
"Yes, and what I'm saying is that DRS is a known solution for that. It's not like something we'd need to invent. We just need to see, A, if we need it, and B, how much of it we would need.

"We clearly don't want to create a situation where cars just fly past each other without any fight, we want there to be racing. We want cars to be entering corners next to each other and fighting, but we have the tools to basically tune it in the right way for 2030."
